annotation.title_clean: Report from the Commission to the European Parliament and the Council adopted pursuant to Article 112(1) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 on the need to review the list of prohibited AI practices and of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III
annotation.title_en: Report from the Commission to the European Parliament and the Council adopted pursuant to Article 112(1) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 on the need to review the list of prohibited AI practices and of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III
annotation.summary_en: First Commission report under Article 112(1) of the EU AI Act assessing whether to amend the Article 5 prohibitions and Annex III high-risk use cases. Drawing on Member State input, a 547-response consultation and AI incident databases, it finds no immediate need to amend, flags a possible gap on CSAM and non-consensual deepfakes, and recommends continued monitoring.
key_provisions_or_claims: Most Member States and stakeholders see no need yet to amend Article 5 or Annex III, given the limited application period.
Potential regulatory gap identified: AI systems generating CSAM and non-consensual intimate deepfakes are not covered by Article 5.
Flagged for monitoring: AI companions and therapy chatbots, emotion recognition, dark patterns, scams, and Annex III point 5 areas.
Annex I product-embedded AI (medical devices, self-driving vehicles) is outside the scope of this review.
Next Article 112 assessment is due in 2026, with coordinated monitoring by the AI Office, the AI Board and national authorities.
